author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read FortiMail history, antispam and antivirus logs, sent to the data collector over syslog. History and antispam logs go to Email and antivirus logs go to Antivirus, while event, system event and encryption logs stay generic.
notes:
Setup:
- Under Log & Report > Log Settings > Remote, send history, antispam and antivirus logs to the data collector over syslog (udp or tcp-legacy for newline framing) with CSV format off.

Field mapping:
- History (type=statistics) logs, one per recipient with the final disposition, and antispam logs go to Email; antivirus logs go to Antivirus.
- Event, system event and encryption logs stay generic.
- disposition and classifier arrive as English text or as hex codes, and both are read.
- The parent's confirm string asks for a FortiMail serial (device_id=FE), because FortiManager writes the same log_id, type and pri keys; in a lab tenant on 2026-10-16 it still took the FortiMail lines in 3 of 5 Run Tests and no FortiManager line in 5, where the old string took both.
- The pairs are read with CEF(), because Sophos NG-SIEM's SPLIT_NAME_VALUES cuts a quoted value that holds " key=" text, such as a subject: in Run Test on 2026-10-16 it cut such a subject, and with CEF() all 99 fields of the samples matched the emulator.
- The engine also stored event_type on the antivirus records, a field its antivirus schema has but the docs' table doesn't list.

Time:
- date and time are in the appliance's zone: the parser uses eventtime or tz when FortiMail sends them (8.0) and otherwise reads the time as UTC.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up from Fortinet's log reference examples.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-13 when it took the lines.
- On 2026-10-14 each child also passed Run Test in a lab tenant as a separate parser under its parent when it took the lines, but the built-in parser still won most runs: the email child took its lines in 5 of 13 Run Tests, the antivirus child in 3 of 5, and the built-in parser took the line only the parent reads both times.

Known gaps:
- The tenant's built-in Fortinet_Master_non-cef parser matches the same lines and normalizes nothing; the engine picks one parser per line, and in a lab tenant on 2026-10-13 the FortiMail parent took the lines in 5 of 12 Run Tests and the combined children in 9 of 24.
- Expect some lines to stay generic.
